Ashwani And 4 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 1 September, 2025

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199793893/
1  HON'BLE VIKAS BUDHWAR, J.

1. Heard Sri Shakil Ahmad, learned counsel for the applicants and Sri S.K. Singh, learned A.G.A. for the State as well as Shri Akhilesh Kumar Yadav, counsel for the opposite party no. 2.
2.

The applicants herein has filed the present application u/s 482 Cr.P.C. for quashing of the summoning order dated 10.11.2023 and Revisional Order dated 24.10.2024 passed in Criminal Revision No.291 of 2024 as well as entire criminal proceedings of Complaint Case No.24038 of 2023, under Sections 498-A, 323, 504, 506 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, P.S. Mahila Thana,
District Bijnor.

3. This Court on 11.12.2024 proceeded to pass the following orders:
"1.
Heard Sri Shakil Ahmad, learned counsel for the applicants and Sri Sunil Kumar Kushwaha, learned A.G.A. for the State.

2. The present 482 Cr.P.C. application has been filed to quash the summoning order dated 10.11.2023 and Revisional Order dated 24.10.2024 passed in Criminal Revision No.291 of 2024 as well as entire criminal proceedings of Complaint Case No.24038 of 2023, under Sections 498-A, 323, 504, 506 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, P.S.
Mahila Thana, District Bijnor.
3. Contention of learned counsel for the applicants is that the applicant no.1 is husband of opposite party no.2 and other applicants are family members of applicant no.1.

The present dispute is a matrimonial dispute between the parties which may be settled through mediation, therefore, this matter may be referred to the Mediation and Conciliation Centre, Allahabad High Court.

4. Issue notice to opposite party no.2.
5.

Considering the nature of the case, the present matter is referred to the Mediation and Conciliation Centre, High Court Allahabad, subject to the condition that the applicants will deposit a sum of Rs.25,000/- within two weeks from today with the Mediation Centre out of which Rs.20,000/- shall be paid to opposite party no.2 on her appearance before the Mediation Centre on a date to be fixed by the Mediation Centre.
Balance Rs.5,000/- shall be retained by the Mediation Centre towards its expenses.

6. After depositing the aforesaid amount within aforementioned time, notices shall be issued to the parties fixing some date for mediation and the Mediation Centre shall make all possible efforts to conclude the mediation and conciliation proceedings expeditiously, preferably within a period of two months.

9. It is made clear that in case there occurs default by the applicants either in depositing the amount or in appearing before the Mediation Centre on the date fixed,

The applicants herein has filed the present application u/s 482 Cr.P.C. for quashing of the summoning order dated 10.11.2023 and Revisional Order dated 24.10.2024 passed in Criminal Revision No.291 of 2024 as well as entire criminal proceedings of Complaint Case No.24038 of 2023, under Sections 498-A, 323, 504, 506 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, P.S. Mahila Thana,
District Bijnor.
The present dispute is a matrimonial dispute between the parties which may be settled through mediation, therefore, this matter may be referred to the Mediation and Conciliation Centre, Allahabad High Court.
Considering the nature of the case, the present matter is referred to the Mediation and Conciliation Centre, High Court Allahabad, subject to the condition that the applicants will deposit a sum of Rs.25,000/- within two weeks from today with the Mediation Centre out of which Rs.20,000/- shall be paid to opposite party no.2 on her appearance before the Mediation Centre on a date to be fixed by the Mediation Centre.
Balance Rs.5,000/- shall be retained by the Mediation Centre towards its expenses.
6. After depositing the aforesaid amount within aforementioned time, notices shall be issued to the parties fixing some date for mediation and the Mediation Centre shall make all possible efforts to conclude the mediation and conciliation proceedings expeditiously, preferably within a period of two months.
8. It is further provided, if applicants file receipt of deposit of the aforesaid amount before the court below then no coercive action shall be taken against the applicants in Complaint Case No.24038 of 2023, under Sections 498-A, 323, 504, 506 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, P.S. Mahila Thana, District Bijnor, till the next date of listing.
9. It is made clear that in case there occurs default by the applicants either in depositing the amount or in appearing before the Mediation Centre on the date fixed,
the interim order shall cease to operate and the Mediation Centre shall immediately communicate to the office which in turn shall list the case within a week before the appropriate Bench for passing orders in the matter.
10.
It is also made clear that in case the applicants fail to submit the receipt of the aforesaid deposit before the court below then the court below is free to proceed against the applicants."
10. Liberty is accorded to the opposite party no. 2 to move appropriate application in case, she is aggrieved.
